thumb.title: India 4-0 Japan. Now World No. 4.
thumb.sub: Best-ever FIH ranking for India's women

slides.sub: A perfect group stage in Bhopal and India's highest FIH ranking ever.

slides.body: India led 3-0 at half-time: Lalremsiami in the 12th minute, Deepika in the 16th, Neha Goyal in the 28th. Deepika added the fourth in the 48th.
slides.note: Japan's best chance was a 35th-minute penalty corner, flicked wide.

slides.title: India's best-ever FIH rankings
slides.note: Two new highs in two days.

slides.body: Wins over Malaysia, Thailand, South Korea, China and Japan. 22 goals scored, 5 conceded.
slides.note: Deepika has 8 goals in the tournament, as reported by RevSportz.

concept: A ranking ladder. The hero puts the challenge in muted grey (Japan were unbeaten too.) and the double payoff in white: a 4-0 win and World No. 4. Slide 2 explains why the game was decided early with one giant 3-0, the half-time score, and the minutes of each goal. Slide 3 is the visual centrepiece: a bar ladder of India's best-ever FIH rankings, 2018 to tonight, with the lit top bar showing No. 4 and the bar above last night's No. 5, so you can see two records fall in two days. Slide 4 sums up the perfect group stage in 5 / 5 and the last slide sets up Friday's semi-final with a question. Indian-sport orange, type and charts only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
Japan were unbeaten too. India won 4-0. Now World No. 4.

India finished the Women's Asian Champions Trophy group stage with five wins from five in Bhopal on Wednesday. Lalremsiami, Deepika and Neha Goyal made it 3-0 by half-time and Deepika added a fourth in the 48th minute.

The win lifts India to No. 4 in the FIH world rankings, their highest ever. They only reached No. 5 for the first time a day earlier after the 6-2 win over China. The previous best was No. 6 in 2022. RevSportz reports India moved past Spain.

India scored 22 and conceded 5 in the group. The defending champions play their semi-final on Friday, against Malaysia as reported by RevSportz.

Can India defend the title in Bhopal? Tell us below.
